claims.head: The Avalanche should tilt the ice
claims.body: The Avalanche have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. Expect the Avalanche to spend more of the night in the Blackhawks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

story.head: The Avalanche should tilt the ice
paras: The Blackhawks (4-9-1) lost 5-4 in overtime to Boston on Saturday, while the Avalanche have won two in a row. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Avalanche third (tied for 13th in the NHL) and the Blackhawks last (31st).

The Avalanche’s record (.607) is about what their chances are worth. The Blackhawks have played better than their record (.321) says: their chances are worth about .384, and their finishing has held them back.

The Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest), play the league’s fastest games (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (2nd). Colorado has scored 4.21 goals a game, the most in the league. The Blackhawks pick their shots (2nd lowest) and don't block many shots (32nd). They also have struggled on the power play (31st), so their struggling power play gets a tough test from the Avalanche’s penalty killers. Chicago has scored 2.21 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 3.79, the third most. The Avalanche are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Hawks.

Nathan MacKinnon (9 G / 15 A / 24 P in 14 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is tied for fourth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. Artturi Lehkonen (12 G / 5 A / 17 P in 14 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for second in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. For the Blackhawks, Connor Bedard (4 G / 5 A / 9 P in 8 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Roman Kantserov (5 G / 2 A / 7 P in 14 GP) has a team-high five goals.
Mackenzie Blackwood (7-3-0 / .897 SV% in 10 GS) will likely start for Colorado, and Spencer Knight (4-7-0 / .897 SV% in 11 GS) for Chicago.
The Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Blackhawks do.
